newsitem.title: UK: Dollar boosted by rates, bourses mixed.
newsitem.headline: Dollar boosted by rates, bourses mixed.

text.p: U.S. economic data surprised financial markets on Thursday by reinforcing the Federal Reserve's decision this week to hold interest rates unchanged.
Wall Street swiftly erased early gains, however, and blue chip stocks moved lower in the first hour of trading.

The dollar pared strong early gains, too, as a surprisingly large drop in durable goods orders in August prompted some traders to question whether there would be any rise in U.S. interest rates this year.

"Durable goods are a volatile figure. But it clearly shows that the economy is losing momentum...and that the Federal Reserve was clearly right in refraining from raising interest rates the other day," Irwin Kellner, chief economist, at Chase Regional Bank in New York said.
Worries over IMF gold sales prompted gold to fix in London at its lowest price since September 6, 1995 at $380.45 an ounce, down from $382.05 at the morning fix.

The fall followed comments from International Monetary Fund head Michel Camdessus that the fund had the necessary majority to sell five million ounces of gold from its reserves to help the world's poorest nations.
The dollar rose strongly in early European trade as the markets reassessed this week's Fed decision and the Swiss made a surprise cut in their own rates.

The dolalr powered a pfennig higher through 1.52 marks as the German currency came under pressure from a series of European units. But by mid-afternoon in Europe, the dollar had shaved some the gains and was hovering around 1.52 marks.
Currency markets were surprised by the Swiss National Bank's decision to hack 0.50 of a percentage point off its discount rate, taking it to 1.0 percent.
Wall Street opened a little higher but the Dow Industrials swiftly went into retreat, losing about 25 points in the first 45 minutes trading.
European markets, which had been cautious ahead of the U.S. data, searched for direction.
German shares held up at near record high levels, but dealers bemoaned weak trading volumes and were divided on whether the market's bull run could continue.
Gains by government bonds following the U.S. data, kept the 30-share IBIS DAX index steady around its opening levels after the DAX ended floor trade up 7.58 points at 2,666.55.
Some dealers warned of impending vertigo, with one Frankfurt dealer saying: "People are starting to get cold feet. I really think we have shot up too quickly."
British shares struggled for direction in thin end-of-quarter trading, but received support from a leap in bonds after the U.S. data.
The FTSE 100 was down about six points at 1415 GMT but above the day's lows on volume of only 375.5 million shares.
Selective profit-taking in retail stocks helped drag the market down, while drugs company Zeneca dropped after Bayer ruled out a bid.
France's blue chip CAC-40 index weakened a few points as some stocks took a hammering from investors after reporting disappointing first-half results.
LVMH fell 3.18 percent on a disappointing rise in first-half profit, while Lyonnaise des Eaux dropped 2.08 percent on disappointing results and cautious outlook.
CURRENCIES AT 1415 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.5203 marks and 110.37 yen, compared with late Wednesday's European level of 1.5112 marks and 110.40 yen.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1415
LONDON - The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was down 6.9 points at 3,928.8.
PARIS - The CAC-40 share index was off 5.73 points at 2,097.68.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index closed up 7.58 points at 2.666.55. In later computerised trade, the IBIS DAX was down 0.87 points at 2,662.23. PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed at its lowest price since September 6, 1995 at $380.45 per ounce, down from $382.05 at the morning fix.
